subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` as core lifecycle phases for sub-agent startup, or solve the hang-like symptom through a narrower internal diagnostic/recovery path?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the proposed fix creates new core lifecycle/API semantics across gateway, session, SDK, and subagent consumers; automation should not choose that contract unilaterally.

options.title: Sponsor lifecycle phases
options.body: Accept the additive event contract and ask for a fresh current-main implementation across embedded-agent, subagent registry, gateway wait/session projection, SDK normalization, docs, and focused proof.

options.title: Narrow to diagnostics/recovery
options.body: Keep public lifecycle phases unchanged and require a smaller fix that makes startup aborts visible or recoverable through existing terminal status and logging surfaces.

options.title: Reject new core surface
options.body: Close the lifecycle-event request and keep related startup failures tracked only by concrete reproductions such as the sandbox-mode issue.

recommendation.title: Sponsor lifecycle phases
recommendation.body: Accept the additive event contract and ask for a fresh current-main implementation across embedded-agent, subagent registry, gateway wait/session projection, SDK normalization, docs, and focused proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main blame and feature history point to steipete around the embedded lifecycle and subagent/session projection surfaces, making him the best available routing owner for the product/API decision.
